definitions.explanation: The area where the upper and lower eyelids meet near the nose. Often referenced in emotional contexts.

examples.japanese: {目頭|めがしら}が{熱|あつ}くなった。
examples.english: My eyes welled up with tears.
examples.notes: Literally 'the inner corners of my eyes got hot.' A common expression for being moved to tears.

examples.japanese: {感動|かんどう}して{目頭|めがしら}を{押|お}さえた。
examples.english: I was so moved that I pressed the corners of my eyes.

examples.japanese: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}で{子|こ}どもの{姿|すがた}を{見|み}て、{思|おも}わず{目頭|めがしら}が{熱|あつ}くなった。
examples.english: Seeing my child at the graduation ceremony, I couldn't help but tear up.

notes:
USAGE: Most commonly appears in the set expression {目頭|めがしら}が{熱|あつ}くなる (to have tears well up, to be moved to tears). This is a more restrained, literary way of expressing being moved than simply saying {泣|な}く.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目頭|めがしら}が{熱|あつ}くなる: to tear up, to be moved to tears
- {目頭|めがしら}を{押|お}さえる: to press the inner corners of one's eyes (to hold back tears)

ANATOMY: Contrasts with {目尻|めじり} (outer corner of the eye).
